items.note: Says exports can reach about 2 million rows, so memory use matters as well as speed.
Keeps the signature export_orders_csv(db, path). It leaves out why (three callers), but the requirement itself is there.
Keeps the header exactly as id,customer_name,total,created_at with the same column order.
Says to add no new dependencies, and adds that the standard library is fine.
Names the per-row customer lookup (N+1) as the main cause. It's framed as the person's diagnosis to confirm, which fits what they said.
Says to write rows to the file as they're produced instead of building one big string.
Says customer names can contain commas, so values must be CSV-quoted, and calls this a deliberate output change.
Says to verify by running the existing tests in tests/test_export.py and showing the command and its output.
Asks for a minimal, targeted change and says not to restructure the module.
